A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Agents’ Room research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original story-generation experiments, automatic metrics, and expert preference judgments, including Table 2 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, a Gemma2-9B-it evaluation, and supplementary findings.

M1.justification: The planning and writing agents, scratchpad, deterministic orchestration, synthetic training procedure, and agent prompts are unchanged. Algorithm 1 gains explanatory comments, without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use TELL ME A STORY for long-form fiction generation. Newly described genres and replacement story examples document the existing dataset; no additional dataset, task, or input scenario is established. The Gemma experiment changes model configuration.

E2.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the comparator set with E2EZS plan, E2EZS reflect, E2EZS decompose, and 2STAGE decompose. These receive automatic scores in Table 2 and direct LLM preference comparisons in Table 3, extending v1’s basic end-to-end baselines to explicit planning, reflection, and decomposition alternatives.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a zero-shot Gemma2-9B-it setting and direct pairwise win-rate reporting. Section 7 adds a longer-story preference calculation excluding ties. Existing dataset splits, Gemini configuration, LoRA training settings, and human evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused checks of story-length preference and robustness to a smaller backbone, plus participant feedback identifying repetition and tone discordance. The original planning-versus-writing ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 3’s error bars, agreement and correlation statistics, and evaluator consistency under reversed presentation order are unchanged. The additions introduce no new seed information, repeated-run practice, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All nine original Table 2 rows and Figure 3 are unchanged. v2 adds four baseline rows and Table 3 overall preference rates of 74.55%, 67.27%, 89.09%, and 66.67% against the four new comparators, respectively. Table 4 adds an 80% overall preference for Agents’ Room with Gemma2-9B-it. The 0.51 longer-story preference and new model outputs and participant feedback further expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The mathematical framework, scratchpad update, orchestrator formulation, and pairwise-comparison calculation are retained. Explaining that V denotes vocabulary tokens adds clarification rather than a new definition or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same claims about collaborative writing, the dataset, specialized-agent training, and evaluation. New experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 uses the length-preference check to argue that human-story preference is not simply a length effect and interprets the Gemma results as extending the observed advantage to smaller models. Appendix F also explains the reliance on backbones with adequate context capacity and writing quality.

D1.justification: v2 announces release of metrics alongside the dataset, describes how the new baselines reuse planning instructions, and identifies the additional Gemma checkpoint. It also adds dataset genre and workshop-process details. Existing training hyperparameters and appendix prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to decomposed prompting, Self-Refine, Reflexion, and Gemma 2 in connection with the new comparisons. References to Schimel and Ricketson and Graham disappear with the introductory academic/news-writing examples. The main related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 trims introductory examples, consolidates paragraphs, adds algorithm explanations, expands the comparison-system passage, and introduces Appendix F. Appendix A is retitled to include system outputs. The main section order and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix A is substantially redesigned from three human-only examples into two matched human/E2E/Agents’ Room sets with markedly smaller text. Figure 1 gains agent labels and the fifth writing-agent icon; Figure 2 replaces its prompts. Table 2 is expanded and regrouped, and Tables 3–4 and a feedback panel are added. Figure 3 remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added planning/reflection controls address a weakness in v1’s comparator set, while the Gemma and length-preference checks improve empirical support. The gains are limited by reliance on LLM judgments for the new comparisons. There is also a small reporting regression: Section 7 retains the old BERTScore interpretation despite the new E2EZS plan row having the highest score, 0.8173.
